title: Before the First Piece Is Set: Approvals, Layout and Plan
summary: Steel goes up safely only if the foundation, site and plan are ready. This talk covers what must be in place and in writing before erection starts.
talking_points: The controlling contractor must give the steel erector written notice that footing, pier and wall concrete (and masonry mortar) has reached 75 percent of the intended minimum compressive design strength, or enough strength to carry erection loads, based on an appropriate ASTM test of field-cured samples (29 CFR 1926.752(a)(1)).
A steel erector must not erect steel until it receives that written notification (1926.752(b)).

The controlling contractor must provide adequate access roads for delivery and movement of cranes, trucks and material, and means of pedestrian and vehicle control, plus a firm, properly graded, drained area close to the work with space for materials and equipment (1926.752(c)).
All hoisting operations must be pre-planned so that no one works under a load except as the rules allow (1926.752(d), 1926.753(d)).

Where an employer elects, due to site-specific conditions, to use the alternate means and methods allowed in 1926.753(c)(5), 1926.757(a)(4) or 1926.757(e)(4), a site-specific erection plan must be developed by a qualified person and be available at the work site (1926.752(e)).
All columns must be anchored by at least four anchor rods, and each column must be evaluated by a competent person to see whether guying or bracing is needed (1926.755(a)(1), (a)(4)).
Columns must be set on level finished floors, pre-grouted leveling plates, leveling nuts or shim packs adequate to transfer construction loads (1926.755(a)(3)).

Anchor rods cannot be repaired, replaced or field-modified without the approval of the structural engineer of record, and the controlling contractor must notify the erector in writing of any such change before the column is erected (1926.755(b), 1926.752(a)(2)).
site_hazards_to_check: Soft, wet or poorly graded laydown area
Anchor rods bent, repaired or modified without approval
Column bases shimmed with inadequate material
discussion_questions: Do we have the written concrete strength notice in hand?
Where is the site-specific erection plan, if we need one?
Who evaluates columns for guying or bracing?
